items.text: Many local towns like Rye and Bexhill give free Saturday parking during the festive season to boost local high streets, but not Hastings. That is why last year I launched a campaign calling on the local council to roll it out in Hastings, too. Does the Leader of the House agree that after the Government took decisive action in the Budget yesterday to support local businesses and cut business rates, Green-run Hastings borough council should get in the festive spirit early and support my campaign for Christmas parking in Hastings?

items.title: Business of the House
items.line: Spoke in "Business of the House" (Commons Chamber): "Reform-run East Sussex county council is responsible for unblocking drains and filling potholes, but too often nothing is done when residents report those issues. I have been shocked to discover that the same contractor, Balfour Beatty, is paid both to indepen"
items.text: Reform-run East Sussex county council is responsible for unblocking drains and filling potholes, but too often nothing is done when residents report those issues. I have been shocked to discover that the same contractor, Balfour Beatty, is paid both to independently check the quality of pothole filling and to fill potholes. I was also shocked to discover today that the number of miles of road that East Sussex is resurfacing this year is down on last year, bucking the national trend, despite extra money from this Labour Government to sort those issues out. Does the Leader of the House agree that Reform-run East Sussex county council must get a grip, fill the potholes and unblock the drains?

items.title: Topical Questions
items.line: Spoke in "Topical Questions" (Commons Chamber): "T7. Many hospital specialisms are increasingly shared between Eastbourne hospital and Hastings Conquest hospital, which is in my constituency. That means that the people I represent who do not drive are required to travel a long way by public transport to get "
items.text: T7. Many hospital specialisms are increasingly shared between Eastbourne hospital and Hastings Conquest hospital, which is in my constituency. That means that the people I represent who do not drive are required to travel a long way by public transport to get to Eastbourne hospital—between 90 minutes and two hours, and that involves a lot of walking. The hon. Member for Eastbourne (Josh Babarinde) shares my concerns about people travelling in the other direction. With so many services shared between the two hospitals, I am calling on the NHS integrated care board, the trust, and the Reform-run county council to look at providing a shuttle bus that would make it easier for people to travel between the two hospitals. Does the Minister agree that this is something health commissioners should look at when planning services?

items.title: International Update
items.line: Spoke in "International Update" (Commons Chamber): "I welcome the Prime Minister’s commitment to strengthening relations with our European neighbours. Can I give him one example of how he can boost economic growth by doing just that on the south coast? Thousands of the people I represent have called for interna"
items.text: I welcome the Prime Minister’s commitment to strengthening relations with our European neighbours. Can I give him one example of how he can boost economic growth by doing just that on the south coast? Thousands of the people I represent have called for international trains to come back to Ashford International. It would boost our economy by £2.7 billion and bring half a million more visitors to Sussex and Kent every year, and we have an international terminal sitting there ready to be used. It is a no-brainer, so will the Prime Minister give me his commitment that he will support this, like the Transport Secretary?

hastings-and-rye.summary: Helena Dollimore is the Labour (Co-op) MP for Hastings and Rye. Of the 26 Commons votes recorded since 3 November 2026, they voted in 26 (100%), always with most Labour (Co-op) MPs. They spoke 5 times in 4 debates (about 676 words); most often in "Business of the House", "International Update" and "Strengthening Community Resilience". They tabled 6 written questions, most often to the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (3) and the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (2). On the 19 votes where both the area's MPs voted, Helena Dollimore and Dr Kieran Mullan voted the same way 2 times and opposite ways 17 times.

During the original negotiation period, every time that the EU was obstinate, stubborn and difficult, Labour Members sought to blame the Conservatives for that, instead of getting behind this country and standing up to that sort of behaviour.

items.text: On employers, there are various, complex ways in which the Government are trying to unpick the damage they did with their tax rises. Big businesses will engage with such projects—they can look at them for use across their entire workforce—but smaller businesses cannot as they do not have the mental thinking space or the time to go through them. We have seen the biggest drop in employment among those smaller businesses—the people who speak to me and tell me how bad things are—but the Government seem to be completely ignoring that.

items.text: I do not think that foreign nationals should be entitled to benefits, because of the basis on which they are allowed into our country. The only reason they are allowed into our country is that they are net contributors. Why would we undermine that by allowing them to be net recipients of benefits? They are only here because they have signed up to the idea that they will come and be net contributors, so I do not think that that entitles them.

items.text: They are citizens, are they not? They have signed a deeper contract with the country that they are in, and they are here under a different set of circumstances. The hon. Member needs to be clearer when she asks her questions in relation to two different groups of people, because we treat them very differently in our proposals. There is a distinction. Let me make a final point that is often not talked about enough. We are all incredibly focused on what the Government should do to help people and how taxpayers should help people. We know that for very many people in poverty, a big factor in that is having absent parents who give them absolutely no money or pitiful amounts of money for very many years. items.title: Topical Questions
items.line: Spoke in "Topical Questions" (Commons Chamber): "The ability of powerful men to exert control over and exploit women is again at the forefront of our minds. But it is not just rich and powerful men: we recently debated in this place a petition by Paris Shears, who campaigns against coercive and controlling b"
items.text: The ability of powerful men to exert control over and exploit women is again at the forefront of our minds. But it is not just rich and powerful men: we recently debated in this place a petition by Paris Shears, who campaigns against coercive and controlling behaviour. During the debate, the Minister refused to give Paris the common courtesy of explaining whether those convicted of coercive and controlling behaviour are eligible for Labour’s early release programme. Can the Justice Secretary show proper respect to Paris and other victims and at least answer that question now?

items.title: Topical Questions
items.line: Spoke in "Topical Questions" (Commons Chamber): "It is obvious that the Minister does not want to put on record and own up to the fact that those convicted of coercive and controlling behaviour are, according to our understanding, eligible for early release. [ Interruption. ] The Minister says from a sedenta"
items.text: It is obvious that the Minister does not want to put on record and own up to the fact that those convicted of coercive and controlling behaviour are, according to our understanding, eligible for early release. [ Interruption. ] The Minister says from a sedentary position that I should read; I will pass it on to Paris that he feels she should have just read. The public want clarity from Ministers on these complex matters, and it is right for me to ask this question. How can the Minister justify releasing those convicted of coercive and controlling behaviour early when we know that perpetrators who go on to commit offences like rape often start out with lower offences, like common assault, coercive and controlling behaviour and grooming. We know the patterns that emerge over time. Surely we should tackle this at the first instance and not let these people out early.

The previous Conservative Government took a number of st"
items.text: It is a pleasure to serve under your chairmanship, Sir Alec. As the Minister has outlined, these two orders make changes to the rules on recording and broadcasting court proceedings, and we support them. The previous Conservative Government took a number of steps to improve the transparency of the courts and to help the public to understand better how judicial decisions are made. Those steps included allowing proceedings in the Court of Appeal to be broadcast and, from 2022, allowing judges’ sentencing remarks in the Crown court to be filmed and broadcast. The aim was straightforward: people should be able to see and better understand how our courts work, while victims, witnesses and defendants continue to receive appropriate protection. These orders build on that approach. It is important to note, as the Minister said, that this is not an unrestricted right to film proceedings. Recordin

items.title: Jackdaw Gasfield
items.line: Spoke in "Jackdaw Gasfield" (Commons Chamber): "We all want to secure the future employment prospects of those working in our world-leading oil and gas sector, and one of the richest possible opportunities for that is transitioning them into working in deep geothermal in constituencies such as mine across t"
items.text: We all want to secure the future employment prospects of those working in our world-leading oil and gas sector, and one of the richest possible opportunities for that is transitioning them into working in deep geothermal in constituencies such as mine across the country. However, despite repeated cross-party meetings with Ministers, going back years now, I am afraid that we are still billions and billions behind the money being invested in this technology in other parts of the world. Does the Minister agree that it would be crazy not to create a set-aside fund, from the money that has been announced today, that is purely dedicated to developing deep geothermal in our country?

items.title: MOD Bicester and Illegal Migrants
items.line: Spoke in "MOD Bicester and Illegal Migrants" (Commons Chamber): "I welcome the opportunity to take part in this debate. The concerns and worries of women in Piddington about the sorts of people being placed alongside them are shared by women up and down the country. You and I, Madam Deputy Speaker, know better than many exa"
items.text: I welcome the opportunity to take part in this debate. The concerns and worries of women in Piddington about the sorts of people being placed alongside them are shared by women up and down the country. You and I, Madam Deputy Speaker, know better than many exactly what those concerns are, because of the camp in Crowborough. The Government have placed more than 500 young men in Crowborough, in your Sussex Weald constituency, and they are pledging to keep them there all the way till 2030. Madam Deputy Speaker has had to do her best in the face of a Green, Lib Dem and Labour council that has totally failed in its responsibilities to support those residents. The contrast in scale at Piddington, where there are just 350 residents, is even greater. At the heart of the debate is whether women have a legitimate, reasonable concern to be worried about the people being placed in their communities.

That is the point: these cultures are worse than ours on the many issues we care about in relation to women and girls. Gentleman has to suggest that no other countries in the world manage to enter into complex legal arr"
items.text: I urge the hon. Gentleman to read Lord Wolfson’s report, which makes it clear that we can engage in international agreements. To make the point valid, the hon. Gentleman has to suggest that no other countries in the world manage to enter into complex legal arrangements without both being part of the ECHR. Of course they do. Agreements will be subject to renegotiation. This country is absolutely right to respond to what our people want us to do, which is to protect our borders and put them first, and not the sorts of people we are putting up at taxpayers’ expense in Crowborough.

bexhill-and-battle.summary: Dr Kieran Mullan is the Conservative MP for Bexhill and Battle. Of the 26 Commons votes recorded since 3 November 2026, they voted in 19 (73%), always with most Conservative MPs. They spoke 40 times in 9 debates (about 7,745 words); most often in "Welfare", "MOD Bicester and Illegal Migrants" and "Topical Questions". They tabled 11 written questions, most often to the Treasury (4) and the Ministry of Justice (3). On the 19 votes where both the area's MPs voted, Dr Kieran Mullan and Helena Dollimore voted the same way 2 times and opposite ways 17 times.
